intended_object: An accessor that sends a point of the fibre `Fiber p b` (the subtype of the Moore replacement `MooreReplacement p` cut out by the condition that the path ends at `b`) to its underlying point of `MooreReplacement p`. The docstring and its use as an API projection (`ext`, `continuous_val`, `target_path_val`) show this.
explanation: The body is just `Subtype.val`, wrapped under a named projection so the library can attach its own simp and ext lemmas (`val_eq_subtypeVal`, `ext`, `target_path_val`, `continuous_val`). It is an implementation detail of the subtype API, not a separate mathematical construction. If it were read as the fibre inclusion F' → E', it would be correct and fully general, since it is literally the subtype inclusion. But it is an unbundled function, and the continuous inclusion is handled separately by `continuous_val`. So it is best classed as a technical device, not a mathematical object.
